issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 5 asserts that when $p = \psl + 1$ and $R(z)$ satisfies (42), the global error achieves superconvergence order $q = \psl + 1$ with a constant $D$ independent of the stiff linear operator $J$. In the proof, the authors define $F(\tau; Z, t) = (I - R(Z))^{-1} \oc[\treevar][Z][t]$ and treat it as a scalar rational function of $z \in \mathbb{C}$, applying the scalar von Neumann inequality (Nevanlinna / Hairer 1982) to conclude that $\|F(\tau; Z, t_n)\|$ is bounded uniformly for $\mu(Z) \le 0$. For vector systems ($N \ge 2$), this reasoning fails because $\oc[\treevar][Z][t]$ contains multilinear derivative terms $g^{(k)}(y(t))$ (such as the Jacobian $g'(y(t))$) interleaved with rational functions of $Z = hJ$. Because $g'$ and $J$ do not commute, $F$ is not a scalar rational function of $Z$. Moreover, for order $p = \psl + 1$ trees with nonlinear vertices, terms of the form $(I - R(Z))^{-1} g' Z$ arise in $F(\tau; Z, t)$. As $h \to 0$, $(I - R(Z))^{-1} \sim -Z^{-1}$, producing $-Z^{-1} g' Z = -J^{-1} g' J$. When $J$ and $g'$ do not commute, $\|J^{-1} g' J\|$ can be arbitrarily large even when $\mu(J) \le 0$ (e.g., $J = \text{diag}(-\epsilon, -1)$ with $\mu(J) = -\epsilon \le 0$ and $g' = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ yields $\|J^{-1} g' J\| = 1/\epsilon \to \infty$). Consequently, $\|F\|$ and the shifted errors $\xi_n$ cannot be bounded independently of $J$, and the claimed superconvergence rate $q = \psl + 1$ does not hold uniformly in stiffness for general semilinear systems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the superconvergence claim $q = \psl + 1$ for general semilinear systems in Theorem 5 and establish $q = \psl$ as the uniform B-convergence rate (or restrict the $q = \psl + 1$ claim to scalar ODEs $N=1$ or linear problems where $g$ is independent of $y$).
issues.overall_effect: The stiffness-independent superconvergence rate $q = \psl + 1$ is unproven and false for general semilinear systems. As a consequence, the guaranteed uniform B-convergence orders for the proposed methods ESDIRK-(8,4,3) ($p=4, \psl=3$) and ESDIRK-(10,5,4) ($p=5, \psl=4$) reduce from 4 and 5 to $\psl = 3$ and $\psl = 4$, respectively.
issues.title: Invalid superconvergence proof and false stiffness-independent global error bound for semilinear systems
issues.why_classification: The superconvergence order $q = \psl + 1$ is a central theoretical guarantee of the paper and the sole justification for the advertised 4th- and 5th-order B-convergence rates of the newly designed methods. Restricting to scalar/linear ODEs or downgrading the convergence order to $q = \psl$ represents a major loss of advertised convergence rates and problem scope.
